labels.notes: UNMARKED, as the dispatch requires (OQ-71 open). A regex over the whole file finds no **`label`** mark. The label appears at l.10 as `bzthm:c2s3t1_poche_balayable` — `benzecri1960_ch2.tex:517`, inside the first 4000 characters. The REPORT status is `partial` with marked=false, which matches. I read the statements against l.517–533 and l.593–620, and checked the transcription of 2°–4° and of the proof of 4° against the scan's page images (journal pp. 254–255 = PDF pp. 27–28). HYPOTHESES (theoreme_poche_balayable and 2°–4°): « variété localement projective » is [ChartedSpace (S n) V] [HasGroupoid V (projGroupoid n)], a weakening (T2 and second countability are dropped). « connexe » is [PreconnectedSpace V], a weakening. « balayable » is IsBalayable (GSR n) (S n) V = IsBalayableFor … ⊤, the weakest form. The pocket is IsPocheProj P l φ z, the strict Déf. 1′. There is no NeZero n, so every dimension is covered. No hypothesis is added. 2° (theoreme_deuxieme): SimplyConnectedSpace ↥P → SimplyConnectedSpace V, exactly as printed. 3° (theoreme_troisieme): IsCoqueProj P l φ z (Déf. 2 = pocket ∧ IsConvexPart (φ '' P), so « φ(P) convexe ») gives Sphere.IsStrictConvexPart (range p) for EVERY developing p with EqOn p φ P. That is stronger than the printed « un convexe », and the assembly projects .1, IsConvexPart. 4° (theoreme_quatrieme): IsCoqueStricteProj gives IsCorpsConvexeS n (closure (range p)) ∧ interior (closure (range p)) = range p, which is the printed « l'intérieur d'un corps convexe » with the witness K named. The assembly states ∃ K, IsCorpsConvexeS n K ∧ range φ' = interior K. In theoreme_poche_balayable, TheoremeComposantePrinted and TheoremePrinted, the conclusions of 2°–4° are stated for range φ', where φ' is the chart of 1° bound by the same ∃, so φ̃ is the paper's φ̃. ASSEMBLIES: TheoremeComposantePrinted n quantifies over V : Type with T2, ConnectedSpace and SecondCountableTopology, every pocket (P, l, φ, z) with Fact (l ≠ 0), and states ∃ φ' (compatible chart, source = univ, EqOn φ' φ P), together with 1° in component form (∀ x ∈ P, P = connectedComponentIn (φ'⁻¹' demiEspace z) x) and 2°, 3° and 4° as printed. That is the printed Theorem with 1°'s second sentence read as a connected component. theoremeComposantePrinted (n : ℕ) proves it for every n. TheoremePrinted n is the same with P = φ'⁻¹'(demiEspace z ∩ range φ'), the printed full form. theoremePrinted_iff : TheoremePrinted n ↔ ConnexePrinted n, where ConnexePrinted is the strict Benzecri.ConnexePrinted from Developpement.lean. It is NOT true by unfolding: an `unfold …; exact Iff.rfl` probe fails. Its → direction goes through premierPrinted_iff (which uses the uniqueness of the chart), and its ← direction needs 2°–4° from theoreme_poche_balayable. MARKABILITY AFTER OQ-71, stated plainly. (a) If the component form is ruled the statement of record, the row is marked on theoremeComposantePrinted with no Lean change; only the docstring gains the mark. (b) If the full form is required, the ruling alone does NOT mark the row. The mark then waits on a proof of ConnexePrinted, which is open, with neither a proof nor a counterexample. Once that proof exists, theoremePrinted_iff gives TheoremePrinted n, so this file needs no change (only a one-line anchor `TheoremePrinted n`). A refutation would make the row a finding, never a mark. The docstring's « either answer … marks the row with no Lean change » overstates case (b): see the findings.

checks.demi_droite_lemma: exists_demiDroite takes C open, nonempty, IsStrictConvexPart and ¬∃ K, IsCorpsConvexeS n K ∧ C = interior K. It gives x, p linearly independent with Sphere.halfLine x p ⊆ C and ±s(x) ∈ frontier C. Sphere.halfLine x p is the set of rays of {a x + b p | b > 0}, the open half great circle bounded by the antipodal points s(x) and s(−x). That is Remarque 1's half-line, and it matches l.606–607's gloss « portion de droite limitée à deux points diamétralement opposés de la frontière de V ». exists_demiDroite_of_ne_univ replaces strict by IsConvexPart ∧ C ≠ univ, which is correct because an open convex part other than S(n) is strict (Sphere.isStrictConvexPart_of_isOpen, true also at n = 0). Both are the right convex-geometry facts. The converse eq_interior_corpsConvexe_iff_not_demiDroite is also correct. univ_not_demiDroite is a fair refutation for V = S(n): it proves IsOpen, IsConvexPart (∪ reading), ¬ interior of a convex body, and frontier univ = ∅, so no end can lie on the frontier. Is φ̃(V) ≠ S(n) proved for every pocket? Yes, in substance. neg_notMem_range_of_poche takes only IsPocheProj (no shell) and gives p N ≠ −p M for all M, N and every developing p with EqOn p φ P. So range p has no antipodal pair, hence range p ≠ univ, a one-step corollary that is not stated as its own lemma. theoreme_troisieme also gives it as strictness.

findings.where: REPORT.json labels[0].findings[0] (« The fact holds exactly for the open convex parts other than S(n) »)
findings.what: This text goes to the author, and as written it is not exact. The empty set is an open convex part other than S(n), is not the interior of a convex body, and contains no half-line, so « exactly » fails at ∅. The Lean lemmas carry hne : C.Nonempty. The failure for S(n) also depends on the reading. S(n) is a convex part in the ∪ reading of Déf. 8 ruled by DEC-120. In the Minkowski reading it is not (F(S(n)) = E∖{0} is not convex), and there 3° would already give V ≠ S(n). The core of the finding is correct and proved: the general fact fails for S(n), the paper does not say why φ̃(V) ≠ S(n), and it holds for every pocket (neg_notMem_range_of_poche).
findings.fix: Write « the nonempty open convex parts other than S(n) ». Add « (Déf. 8 in the ∪ reading, DEC-120) » after « S(n) is an open convex part ».

findings.where: REPORT.json labels[0].findings[1] (« these are segments of V because φ̃(V) is convex (3°) »)
findings.what: In the paper's argument, L ⊆ V is given, so gL ⊆ V, and every closed sub-arc (gM, X) of the half-line gL is a segment of V without 3°. Convexity is sufficient, and the Lean proof happens to use it. It is not the reason, and the sentence suggests that 4° needs 3° at this step. The finding is also a simplification of the route (no g is needed), not a defect of the paper.
findings.fix: Write « these are segments of V because they lie on gL ⊆ V ». Keep the item labelled as an exposition remark.
